product_offering.core_offering: Increase operates an enterprise-grade, API-first banking platform that gives technology companies direct programmatic access to U.S. payment and banking rails (FedACH, Fedwire, FedNow, Visa, Mastercard, and The Clearing House RTP). The platform exposes bare-metal primitives for storing, moving, and reconciling money, plus a unified API and dashboard to monitor balances and transactions in real time. Increase partners with Federal Reserve member banks to sponsor the programs it powers.
product_offering.differentiator: Increase differentiates by offering bare-metal, direct-to-network API access rather than abstracted banking layers. It provides transparent data, fewer dependencies, stability and redundancy, and faster build times. The company operates as a standalone parallel core, eliminating dependencies on legacy bank core systems for both fintech companies and banks.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Direct access to FedACH, Fedwire, Check 21, RTP, FedNow, and Visa networks. Same-day ACH by default hitting every Fed window. Real-time settlement tracking from the Federal Reserve. Automatic correlation of ACH and Check returns. Instant virtual and physical card issuance with real-time authorization control. Push-to-card transfers to billions of eligible Visa and Mastercard cards. FDIC insurance access via IntraFi network for deposits. Flexible account structures with unlimited account numbers for reconciliation. Custom compliance programs tailored to specific businesses.
product_offering.problem_solved: Technology companies building financial products face limitations with traditional banking infrastructure that abstracts away network complexity. Increase enables them to programmatically store, move, and reconcile money by connecting directly to Federal Reserve networks (FedACH, Fedwire, FedNow), The Clearing House RTP network, and Visa, providing bare-metal API access with full visibility into payment lifecycles, real-time authorization control, and flexible account structures.
quantifiable_outcome: Increase customers store and send billions of dollars per month through the platform.
product_offering.product_overview: Increase is an enterprise-grade banking API platform providing a unified suite of payment and banking primitives for technology companies. The core platform consists of 8 payment products: ACH (FedACH), Bank Accounts, Cards (Visa), Checks (Check 21), FedNow, Real-Time Payments (RTP), Push-to-Card (Visa Direct/Mastercard Send), and Wires (Fedwire). These are complemented by 7 solution modules—Bill Pay, Payroll, Wallets, Embedded Lending, Fund Administration, Vertical SaaS, and Sponsor Banking—that address specific use cases built on top of the core APIs. The platform connects directly to Federal Reserve networks and major financial networks (Visa, The Clearing House), offering bare-metal API access rather than abstracted complexity, with a focus on transparent data, stability, and faster build times.

The dedicated Bill Pay solution targets platforms that originate or pay bills on behalf of businesses, requiring compliance-grade controls (OFAC screening, sanction lists) and unique per-customer accounts for transparent reconciliation.

icp.primary_use_case: Programmatic bill funding, disbursement, and reconciliation through unique per-customer accounts.
icp.target_buyer: Bill payment platforms and B2B accounts-payable/receivable software providers

icp.buyer_persona: Head of Product, CTO, VP Operations

The Payroll solution bundles ACH, RTP, FedNow, and Push-to-Card so platforms can pay W-2 employees and 1099 contractors from a single ledger, with separation of funds for tax withholdings.

icp.primary_use_case: Issuing payroll and contractor payouts across ACH, real-time rails, and push-to-card with unified ledger and tax account separation.

icp.buyer_persona: Head of Product, CTO, Head of Banking Operations

recent_move.description: Launched Push-to-Card transfers, enabling instant fund delivery to eligible Visa and Mastercard cards via Visa Direct and Mastercard Send, extending the platform's instant-payment surface into the card network layer.
Hired Warren Brown as General Manager of card issuing solutions, signaling a dedicated executive owner for the card vertical in conjunction with the Push-to-Card launch.
Accepted into Y Combinator (August 2020), providing initial capital and validation to seed the company founded that same year.
Launched the Sponsor Banking solution, repositioning the platform as a standalone parallel core for traditional banks to connect with fintechs, opening a new customer segment beyond fintechs.

Built a multi-bank sponsor network spanning Grasshopper Bank, First Internet Bank of Indiana, Twin City Bank, and Core Bank, broadening FDIC-insured deposit coverage and card-issuing capacity under a single platform.

Completed annual audits maintaining PCI DSS Level I Service Provider status and SOC 2 Type 2 attestation, reinforcing the compliance posture required to retain sponsor-bank and enterprise fintech relationships.

leadership_change.description: Increase announced the hiring of Warren Brown as General Manager of its card issuing solutions as part of the expansion of its instant payment solutions to include push-to-card transfers.
leadership_change.title: Hiring of Warren Brown as General Manager

expansion_highlight.description: May 2026 Push-to-Card launch plus hiring Warren Brown as GM of card issuing represents a deliberate vertical investment, signaling deeper commitment to card-based payment volumes and potential white-label card program expansion.

Sponsor Banking solution targets traditional banks as a new customer segment, allowing Increase to monetize the same core infrastructure a second time through bank-fintech intermediation rather than only direct fintech clients.

Solution modules for Embedded Lending, Fund Administration, and Vertical SaaS extend the API surface into adjacent fintech verticals beyond the initial bill pay and payroll wedge, broadening addressable use cases.

Push-to-Card documentation references "billions of eligible cards domestically and internationally," and Mastercard Send integration is positioned as an international reach channel, suggesting cross-border card-push as a forward expansion vector.

Warren Brown hire as a dedicated GM for card issuing is the only disclosed senior executive addition, indicating targeted organizational buildout around the card vertical rather than broad-based hiring.
